<!-- Hey there. Thank you so much for improving NewPipe, and filling out the details. Having roughly the same layout helps everyone considerably :)-->

#### What is it?
- [ ] Bugfix (user facing)

#### Description of the changes in your PR
This PR adds a switch to video&audio settings that, when enabled, causes the main player to start automatically in fullscreen mode. This was rather painful to implement, but I think this finally works well.

#### Fixes the following issue(s)
Fixes #4152

Well, firstly a bug: the latest APK pauses videos as soon as they start. This tends to be useful in certain cases, but a problem in most others.

---
Regarding the auto full screen behaviour: is there no way to let the player detect the video orientation and _then_ go into full screen, rotating if needed? Or is that too late in the process?

The current behaviour of the PR, though not optimal, is at least _equivalent_ to the one present in 0.19.x. Even back then, if you came across a portrait video among all the landscape ones, you would have to toggle the orientation at least once. The same thing happens here. You have to tap the full screen button once to go into full screen portrait mode.

Some odd behaviour (which actually ends up helping instead of hurting): Tapping the full screen button while a portrait video is being played in landscape corrects the orientation of full screen to portrait, without going back to the embedded player in the middle. From that point, tapping the button keeps switching between portrait full screen and portrait embedded player.

So from my point of view, at this stage this PR is at least _functionally_ restoring the 0.19.x behaviour, which is great.

If there could be a way to automatically go into full screen, but in the correct orientation without any user interaction, that would be out of this world.

> @avently: I'm curious where all these people who screams about auto fullscreen here and there? So when somebody really doing something that they're asking of they just keep silence. It gives fully understanding that such people is here for screaming (not for real profit of the app). This is what I was confident in since the beginning. If you give power to them (I mean if you do something you don't like just because they ask) it would make the app worse only. Just a sidenote.

I'm quite new on github, so I wasn't one of those people who screamed about "auto fullscreen". But I was one of the fellow users who were really sad with the loss of this feature. It may look like a few more extra clicks, but when you multiply it with the number of videos you watch, it becomes very inefficient.

So, I'm just reassuring you: This actually is a really good feature and is totally worth the effort. Thanks to everyone who contributed to this ❤️

I know this will probably be seen as "yet another user complaining about *that* problem", but I wanted to explain briefly why the auto-full-screen functionality as it was in 0.19.x was so valuable, at least in my case.

My phone is cheap and..... not particularly great. In particular, the touch screen isn't very accurate. Tapping on the video thumbnail to begin full-screen playback was great - a simple one-tap operation. Tapping on the thumbnail *and then* needing to tap on the full-screen icon is much, much more difficult. I often have to tap two or three times before it has registered, and by the time it enters full screen I have missed the first 5 or so seconds of the video.

It's coming up on 9 months since version 0.20 was released, and I still haven't "adapted" to this new workflow - every time I have to play a video, the lack of an ability to tap the thumbnail and have the video start playing in full screen feels really clumsy to me. I completely agree with the points raised about avoiding disrupting new users of the 0.20.x release by making this a default-off feature, but I also think that by excluding the feature entirely the UX is reduced for the (possibly small) subset of users who would appreciate this feature.

Having said all the above, I do realise the pressures that the NewPipe team are under. This is a hugely popular project, and you are doing a commendable job putting out regular releases. The last thing I want to do is burden you with extra work for an issue that probably only affects a small (but vocal!) number of users. Reading through this pull request has made me realise how much more complex such features are - supporting tablets and Android TV was something that never even occurred to me!

I do know a bit of Java, but have never done Android programming. I suppose the first question to try and get this resolved would be to ask @opusforlife2 and @Stypox about how complete this PR was when work seemed to stop in April. With all the new features added since then, is merging this PR still feasible? (I see the GitHub UI is warning of quite a few conflicts).

Would be indeed awesome if this pr could be finished and then merged in the near future. Waiting for this since ages. 😃👌

Since i wanted to donate to newpipe anyways soon (for the awesome work that is done here by the developers of this app) :

I hereby offer to donate 25€ as soon as this feature will be completed and merged. 😀
I love this code! The detailed comments make it easy to understand ❤️ THAT'S how it should be done!
Please use JavaDoc
